message.content: The t9 probe is back. Results: all cases were fully deterministic across 10 repeated runs on identical inputs, and perm was always a valid permutation with gather-consistent sorted_keys. However, there are deterministic mis-sorts (dup_W3/W5/W7, W=6 rand) — but these are reproducible, not nondeterministic, and are explained by the deterministic `(partner < W)` gating in `should_take_partner` for masked lanes, not by stale partner reads. So the visibility claim (c1) is not supported: no nondeterminism observed, and the observed mis-ordering has a deterministic source-level cause. I'll finalize c1 as rebutted, with the mis-sort data preserved for the Judge.

So sorted_keys mismatch on non-power-of-two W and W=6 (rand) suggests actual corruption. That belongs to other claims (c2, c3) but they were not recorded (ledger only has c1). The skeptic's two other claims failed to record. I should finalize c1 (determinism + deterministic but wrong order? No — sorted keys are equal values under ties; sorted_keys wouldn't differ under tie order changes. dup_W3 perm row0 == ref row0 yet sorted mismatch means some other row's sorted keys differ from reference sorted keys — a genuine mis-sort. But cause could be comparator asymmetry (line 43-44 gating with partner<W) — e.g. when partner >= W, in-range lane never swaps even if should — that breaks bitonic for non-power-of-two W. That's a deterministic defect, not a visibility issue. So c1 (visibility/stale reads) — deterministic across 10 runs, no nondeterminism; the wrong-order cases are explainable by a deterministic logic bug, not staleness. So the visibility claim is not confirmed; evidence can't fully separate. I'll mark c1 inconclusive? Or rebutted: no nondeterminism observed, and mis-sorting is deterministic and explained by source-level logic (partner<W gating).
